title: Temporal sampling and lifecycle trace playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
-------
This playbook describes a reproducible approach for sampling runtime requests over time and correlating lifecycle traces (request ingestion -> scheduler -> kernel execution -> response) to support causal profiling, SLO attribution, and compact trace stores. It codifies sampling policies, instrumentation requirements, acceptance criteria for sample quality, and step-by-step ops procedures for running controlled sampling experiments in production and staging.

Why this matters
----------------
- Full-trace capture for every request is too expensive: high cardinality and storage costs.
- Poor sampling biases lead to missed regressions and incorrect SLO triage.
- Temporal sampling tied to lifecycle signals lets us: isolate kernel regressions, measure pre- and post-degradation deltas, and replay realistic sequences in benchmark labs.

Goals and scope
---------------
- Reduce end-to-end trace volume while preserving causal attribution for 95th/99th latency contributors.
- Provide a standard sampling configuration that teams can adopt across dev, canary, and prod environments.
- Ensure sampled traces contain a minimum set of spans and annotations (see "Minimum trace contract" below).
- Document operational runbook for enabling/disabling sampling policies, validating sample health, and performing trace-driven experiments.

Minimum trace contract (required fields in a sampled trace)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) request_id (global UUID)
2) ingest_timestamp and ingest_node id
3) scheduler-arrival & scheduler-dispatch spans with kernel_hint attribute
4) kernel-execution span(s) with kernel_name, kernel_version, and gpu_affinity tags
5) kvcache/kv-prefetch spans (if used) with hit/miss indicator
6) response_timestamp and final_status code
7) cost_estimate.tokens and sequence_length metadata

Sampling strategies (policy catalog)
----------------------------------
- Time-bound uniform (TB-uniform): keep 1 in N requests uniformly across wall-clock time per route. Good for baseline telemetry.
- Probabilistic priority-weighted (PPW): sample with probability p(route, priority) where priority is derived from token-count or customer tier. Useful to bias toward expensive or high-value requests.
- Burst-capture window (BCW): on detection of a latency spike for a cohort, enable 100% sampling for X minutes for that cohort. Use for rapid root-cause windows.
- Horizon-shot correlated sampling (HSCS): sample one request per session-length bucket per user/session to preserve sequence continuity for long-running dialogues.
- Deterministic replay anchor (DRA): tag a small stable fraction of requests (e.g., 0.1%) with a persistent seed so they are consistently captured across both prod and bench replay pipelines.

Recommended default policy (production)
--------------------------------------
- Per-route TB-uniform base rate: 1/500 (0.2%) for low-traffic routes, 1/200 for medium, 1/50 for high-latency or high-cost routes.
- PPW multiplier: +3x for requests with token_count > 512 or from enterprise-tier customers.
- BCW: automatically enabled for 10 minutes when 99th latency for a route exceeds 2x expected baseline.
- DRA: persistent seed with 0.1% global capture rate for deterministic replay.

Instrumentation checklist
------------------------
- SDKs must annotate traces with the minimum trace contract keys above.
- All scheduler nodes must propagate kernel_hint and kernel_version to the downstream kernel agent.
- Kernel agents must emit precise start/end timestamps with GPU cardinality (e.g., gpu_index, nvlink hops).
- A lightweight per-request summary (JSON) should be emitted to a short-lived sampling buffer before full trace ingestion to power fast validation. Example summary: 

  {"request_id":"uuid","route":"/generate","tokens":124,"sequence_len":256,"kernel":"sharded-attn-v2","latency_ms":123.4,"sample_flag":"DRA-1"}

Storage and retention guidelines
-------------------------------
- Full traces: retain for 30 days in hot store (for on-call and triage). After 30 days, move to cold archive for 12 months if flagged by DRA or enterprise customer.
- Summaries: retain for 90 days in time-series store for quick dashboards and sampling health metrics.
- Replay corpus: extracted deterministic seeds (DRA) persist indefinitely until retired by experiment owners.

Quality and acceptance criteria for a sampling run
------------------------------------------------
- Coverage: sampled traces must collectively cover at least 95% of kernel variants observed in a 24-hour window for the route under test.
- Freshness: median time from trace emission to availability in the triage UI must be < 2 minutes for BCW windows, < 10 minutes for baseline samples.
- Causality completeness: >98% of sampled traces must contain all spans in the minimum trace contract.
- Replayability: at least 90% of DRA-tagged traces must be usable in the replay harness (i.e., no missing session context or input truncation).

Metrics and dashboards to build
-----------------------------
- Sampling health dashboard (per-route): sample_rate, sample_coverage (kernel variant coverage), missing_fields_pct, ingest_delay_p50/p95/p99.
- BCW incident dashboard: recent windows, top contributing kernels, request surface heatmap.
- Replay readiness: DRA integrity, replay-success-rate, input-normalization-delta.

Runbook: enabling a BCW capture after an incident
------------------------------------------------
1) Detect spike: alert triggers when 99th latency > 2x baseline for 5m.
2) Triage owner confirms cohort and scope via the incident channel.
3) From sampling control UI or CLI, enable BCW for the affected route with duration 10m and collect full traces. CLI example:

  redwood-samplectl enable --route "/generate" --policy bcw --duration 10m --reason "post-incident triage" --owner "oncall-team"

4) Validate: ensure summaries appear in sampling buffer and full traces start arriving in triage UI within 2 minutes.
5) Collect candidate traces (tag as "incident-YYYYMMDD") and export to bench replay: 

  redwood-replay export --tags incident-20250109 --format ndjson --output s3://redwood-labs/incident-replays/2025-01-09

6) After window expires, automatically revert sampling rates to base policy. Confirm revert with: 

  redwood-samplectl status --route "/generate"

Operational safety and cost controls
----------------------------------
- Global safety cap: no more than 5% of aggregate traffic may be sampled with full traces at any time without explicit approval.
- Per-tenant override must be gated to enterprise-ops and logged in the audit trail.
- Sampling control operations require two-person approval for changes that increase global sampled traffic above 1%.

Experiment checklist (profiling-run)
-----------------------------------
1) Define hypothesis and acceptance metrics (e.g., identify kernel X causing >10ms regression at 99th).
2) Select route(s) and timeframe; choose sampling policy (BCW recommended for incident drilling).
3) Reserve ephemeral storage quota for full traces and ensure RBAC for export.
4) Run sampling for defined window and monitor sampling health dashboard.
5) Export corpus to bench and run replay; capture microbenchmarks for kernel candidates.
6) Document findings and if required, open a kernel regression ticket (include DRA seeds and representative traces).

Common pitfalls and mitigations
------------------------------
- Pitfall: skewed sampling where only low-latency requests are captured (usually due to client-side propensity).
  Mitigation: enforce server-side sampling decision paired with a short deterministic hash of request_id to avoid client bias.
- Pitfall: missing kernel_version tag in legacy agents.
  Mitigation: deploy lightweight agent shim that backfills version from environment metadata and mark shimged traces for review.
- Pitfall: replay failures caused by truncated session context.
  Mitigation: copy the session-window preceding the captured request (HSCS) to the replay corpus.

Telemetry schema (recommended fields)
------------------------------------
| field | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| request_id | string | global UUID used to join traces |
| route | string | API route |
| tokens | integer | token count for generation call |
| sequence_len | integer | input sequence length |
| kernel_name | string | canonical kernel identifier |
| kernel_version | string | semantic version / build id |
| gpu_index | string | physical device index |
| latency_ms | float | wall-clock duration end-start |
| sample_policy | string | e.g., TB-uniform, BCW, DRA |

Backward compatibility and rollout notes
--------------------------------------
- Phase 1 (staging): enable TB-uniform sampling at 1/1000 with full trace capture and validate contract.
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy server-side deterministic sampler and DRA tagging to 5% of nodes. Run 7-day smoke.
- Phase 3 (prod): flip default policy, monitor cost, and enable BCW autopilot. Keep feature flag for rapid rollback.

Ownership and escalation
-----------------------
- Sampling infra owner: Observability / Runtime telemetry team (primary on-call).
- Experiment owner: service team that requested the sampling run.
- Escalation path: oncall -> runtime-infra lead -> SRE director.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets and examples
-----------------------------------------
- Show current sampling policy for a route:
  redwood-samplectl get --route "/generate" --json

- Temporarily increase DRA seed rate:
  redwood-samplectl set --global-dra-rate 0.002 --approve

- Lightweight summary emit (example code, Python):
  import json
  summary = {"request_id": req.id, "route": req.path, "tokens": tokens, "kernel": kernel.name, "latency_ms": latency}
  print(json.dumps(summary))

- Export statement for bench replay (NDJSON):
  SELECT * FROM sampling_buffer WHERE tag = 'incident-20250109' INTO 's3://redwood-labs/incident-replays/2025-01-09/part-000.ndjson' FORMAT NDJSON;

Revision history
----------------

- 2024-12-05: added BCW autopilot thresholds and acceptance criteria (Diego Martinez).
- 2025-01-12: formalized storage retention and added DRA replay integrity requirements (Lena Zhou).
